Seedance 2.5 Prompt Copilot
Purpose

Turn an approved brief and reference pack into one controllable Seedance 2.5 prompt, a complete timecoded audiovisual plan, and a selective review or repair loop. Cover specialist domains through references rather than separate public skills.

Mandatory Preflight Form

This is a hard authorization gate. On every invocation, the first substantive action must be show_form before research, routing, planning, prompt writing or rewriting, diagnosis, reference selection, editing, or generation. There are no clear-brief, direct-generation, quick-answer, or user-urgency exceptions.

Inspect the conversation, canvas, attachments, source media, and previous approved answers first. Then show a compact form in the user's language:

Brief confirmation — required radio with Confirm and continue (Recommended) first and Needs changes second. Summarize the inferred goal, audience, destination, and deliverable.
Duration or scope — required; confirm the exact video duration or exact non-generation output scope.
Reference jobs — required; list every detected reference and its proposed role. Default the take to 全能参考, and for that route name what each non-asset still may lend and must not. Offer First/last-frame mode when the unit is interpolation or the user asked to lock endpoints; those stills are the opening and terminal pictures, not 仅供参考.
Acceptance and risk — required; confirm the primary visible success test and the highest-risk lock: identity, product/SKU, geometry, exact copy, dialogue, rights, evidence, safety, localization, disclosure, or end state.

Set submit_label to the localized equivalent of Confirm and continue. Always use show_form. Never substitute a plain-text questionnaire, ask_question, or show_widget. End the turn immediately after the form and wait. Only a real, non-skipped structured submission referencing that form authorizes the skill to continue. A skip, close, timeout, unrelated reply, or tool error is not approval. Reissue a shorter form when necessary. If show_form is unavailable, stop and report that required confirmation cannot be collected.

Show a new form before continuing when the user changes the brief, duration, mode, references, locks, or acceptance criterion.

Default Multi-Reference Mode

Start every invocation in multi-reference mode. This is the creative default, not a claim about live reference count or compatibility.

Build an ordered Reference Role Map before prompt writing.
Give each source one primary authority: identity/product/IP; setting/geometry; storyboard/shot order; motion/performance/camera; style/material/light; dialogue/voice/music/rhythm; source video/edit scope; or evidence/copy.
Group large packs by role and priority. A published maximum is a ceiling, not a target; use full compatible reference coverage for every fact that must remain stable. One cast is one sheet; complementary assets are different jobs (sheet, plate, board), not several singles of the same face.
Never silently omit, merge, reorder, or reduce a relevant reference to prose; exclude only conflicting sources or true duplicates that add no visible evidence.
Resolve conflicts only after confirmation: user locks; identity/product/copy; geometry and state; storyboard/order; motion/camera; audio; style; atmosphere.
If the pack is incomplete, keep 全能参考 and request the missing sheet or plate, or approval for named placeholders. Do not invent references.
In 全能参考, every still that is not the asset is 仅供参考: the prompt names what it may lend and what it must not. An undeclared still is read as a frame.
First/last-frame mode is a native route: the two stills own opening and terminal composition, and the prompt matches them. Do not rewrite that route as 仅供参考. Attachment count never implies it.

For direct generation, preserve the approved mode, reference order, and prompt. Let the live runtime resolve the exact Seedance 2.5 request mode. If validation rejects the pack, do not drop assets or switch modes; show a new form with valid alternatives.

Runtime Boundary

tapnow-cli owns current model IDs, modes, duration, resolution, input types, reference limits, editing controls, parameters, price, availability, submission, and result state. Public Seedance pages and community workflows inform prompt design only.

Before generation:

read the exact live Seedance 2.5 contract;
resolve all confirmed media;
validate mode, pack, duration, and parameters;
submit the exact final prompt and reference order unchanged;
inspect the returned result.

If the exact model is unavailable, deliver the approved prompt, storyboard, or edit package and report the gap. Never silently substitute Seedance 2.0 or another model. Do not expose internal commands or payloads to users.

Workflow
After form authorization, identify the primary acceptance family: reference orchestration; first/last-frame; story/previs/performance; commercial/growth; knowledge/enterprise/localization; factual/regulated; spaces/mobility/travel; or local editing/repair.
Load only the matching references from the router.
Build the Reference Role Map, immutable-lock list, and conflict notes.
Choose one outcome, a causal event sequence, camera and cut grammar, audio hierarchy, and concrete ending state.
Write a contiguous timeline covering the confirmed duration. Fill the 30-second window when the piece can; every planned shot that fits is a range. Do not cap the take at three shots.
Assemble the final prompt from references/10-prompt-architecture.md.
Review reference influence, continuity, action order, audio, truth, rights, disclosure, and delivery format.
Repair only the failed region, segment, or instruction; keep passed layers.

Timeline Control

Every final generation or video-edit prompt must include a visible Timeline with contiguous ranges formatted exactly like 【0:00-0:03】.

Start at 0:00, cover the full confirmed duration, leave no gaps or overlaps, and end exactly at the confirmed duration.
Give each range one dominant event and resulting state. Include camera, cut or transition, synchronized audio/dialogue, and relevant preserve lock.
Allocate time by complexity rather than equal blocks. Preserve anticipation, contact, reaction, recovery, and a readable final hold.
Place exact dialogue, lyrics, UI events, claims, impacts, match cuts, and beat cues inside their owning range.
For source-video edits, separate source timecodes from output ranges and state their mapping.
For longer sequences, use more ranges rather than overloading each range — and keep them in one generation while they fit the 30-second window.
Treat timeline control as direction, not a runtime guarantee.

Canonical shape:

Prompt Rules
Put reference binding before creative prose. Name what each image, video, audio, storyboard, script, or model controls.
Describe visible events in temporal order and give each action a result.
State subject/object/camera spatial relationships when interaction or geometry matters.
Use one primary camera intent per range; cuts must reveal new information.
Preserve exact user dialogue, lyrics, visible copy, labels, and legal lines.
Separate dialogue, ambience, physical effects, diegetic music, and audience-only score.
Use white-model references to preserve solved space/camera/action while changing surface and light; use green-screen references for isolated motion or performance transfer.
Treat a storyboard as ordered shot logic, not a style collage.
For factual or regulated work, generated visuals illustrate approved sources; they do not become evidence.
Never put unverified provider limits or unsupported parameters into the prompt.
Output Contract

Return:

Creative intent and primary acceptance criterion.
Confirmed setup — duration, destination/aspect when known, mode, locks.
Reference Role Map — every source in confirmed order and its authority.
Timeline — complete contiguous ranges.
Final Seedance 2.5 prompt — one exact prompt, not several competing drafts.
Review checklist — observable reference, continuity, truth, and delivery checks.
Controlled retry — one variable or local region to change.

For direct generation, hand the exact prompt and pack to runtime. For diagnosis, name the visible failure, likely causal instruction, smallest local repair, preserve list, and one retry variable.

Quality Bar
Protect full compatible reference coverage; use roles and priorities to make a rich pack legible, not to prune needed visual evidence.
Make reference authority, event order, and ending state explicit.
Use a storyboard, blockout, or motion source when words cannot control the spatial or temporal problem.
Keep product, identity, copy, evidence, rights, safety, and geometry source-owned.
Use local repair for local failure; do not regenerate a passed sequence.
Separate generated concept from captured gameplay, real UI, verified facts, architectural truth, medical instruction, or current destination conditions.
Do not turn first-party marketing, community popularity, or a single preview into a TapNow runtime or repeatability claim.

name: opus55-motion-icon
text:
返回
opus55-motion-icon

opus55-motion-icon

TapNow

Use when a TapNow Agent user asks Opus 5.5 to create a small animated icon or looping icon video from a prompt or still, including UI, product, technology, brand, or data motifs, and the result must be deterministic, browser-rendered, FFmpeg-encoded, and no longer than 5 seconds.

Opus 5.5 Motion Icon

Create one small, readable animated icon as deterministic HTML/CSS/JavaScript, record it frame by frame in headless Chromium, encode it with FFmpeg, and only call the result a delivered video after media checks pass. The icon may represent an interface control, product feature, device, material, technology concept, brand mark, data motif, or another supplied subject. The output is a motion icon, not a full scene, a website, or a game integration.

Route and preflight

Use exactly one route: Motion icon. Ask only for missing information that changes the implementation or acceptance check. Return a compact preflight before coding:

subject and source: a prompt, an approved still, or a supplied asset path;
runtime/model: confirm the active model is Opus 5.5 (or record model identity as unavailable); do not silently fall back to another model;
one physical motion sentence and its strategy (native, event, part, or surface);
palette, background/alpha requirement, canvas size, and target surface;
duration and FPS, with the hard maximum shown as 5.000s;
source, font, logo, and audio rights or explicit evidence gaps;
output files and one acceptance check.

Do not claim that Opus 5.5, another model, a renderer, browser, encoder, Canvas exporter, or asset is available until the runtime actually exposes it. If the active model cannot be identified, label the model as unverified rather than calling the run an Opus 5.5 execution. A plan, an HTML URL, a browser Blob, or a preview tab is not a verified MP4.

Hard limits

These rules cannot be relaxed to make a render easier:

0 < duration <= 5.000s for every mode. Default/spec mode is exactly 5.000s, 120 BPM, 500ms/beat, 60fps, and 300 encoded frames.
Never render a frame after the last index (0..299 in spec mode). Do not add a tail frame, fade-out tail, trailing audio, or an extra loop frame.
Every final FFmpeg command has an explicit finite -t <duration>. Use finite apad=pad_dur=<seconds> only; never use bare/infinite apad, infinite loops, or a gateway timeout as the stopping mechanism.
The production composition is deterministic. Every animated property is derived from t and stable inputs; no wall-clock time, unseeded randomness, hidden accumulated physics, or non-reproducible camera drift.
seek(0) and seek(duration) settle to the same subject geometry, silhouette, label/title, color, and spring values. The encoded last frame is at (frameCount - 1) / FPS; the conceptual end state is checked separately.
Headless Chromium screenshots and FFmpeg encoding are mandatory for a video deliverable. If either is unavailable, stop at an HTML preview and report the blocker instead of substituting an unverified recording.

If a shorter duration is explicitly requested, recompute the beat interval and slot count in the preflight. Do not describe a shorter cut as 10 x 500ms and do not exceed the cap to preserve a beat grid.

Approval gates

When the user supplies only a prompt, generate exactly one still first. Show it and ask whether the static design is approved. On approval, propose exactly one motion in plain physical language and wait for approval before spending on motion or a full render. If the user supplied an already-approved still, skip only the still approval gate. Do not generate a comparison grid unless the user asks for variants.

Translate ordinary motion language into:

Question	Choice
What happens when left alone?	native for self-moving matter; event for an inert object performing an action; part for one loose or hinged part; surface for light/material moving across a fixed form.
How much does the body move?	still, calm, lively, or playful; use the smallest energy that reads at icon size.
Does the action throw something off?	Add a small emit detail only when the supplied subject supports it; it must return, settle, or be reabsorbed before the loop.

Prefer motion in the subject's own details over a turntable spin. Do not let the whole icon drift out of frame. A squash, recoil, hinge, fill, sweep, reveal, or material response is acceptable when it returns to the opening state.

Default 5-second beat grid

Use this abstract grid for icons and map the subject's own action onto it. The slots are fixed in spec mode; they are not permission to add scenes or a second subject.

Time	Beat	Icon event
0.0s	1	Resting opening pose; this is the loop frame.
0.5s	2	Anticipation, compression, or a small pre-action detail.
1.0s	3	Primary action begins.
1.5s	4	Primary action reaches its readable peak.
2.0s	5	The subject settles while a secondary detail responds.
2.5s	6	A controlled overshoot, hinge, fill, or material change.
3.0s	7	The secondary detail resolves; keep the main silhouette legible.
3.5s	8	Highlight, small emission, or surface pass, only if physically justified.
4.0s	9	Action resolves and the subject returns toward rest.
4.5s	10	Final settle into the opening pose.
5.000s	loop	Same settled state as 0.0s; do not encode frame 301.

For a shorter mode, show the revised grid and receive confirmation before writing the implementation. Do not move events to create extra time; compress the state.

Deterministic implementation

Prefer one self-contained HTML file unless the target runtime requires another stack. Expose testable functions with this shape (adapt names to the source):

The interactive preview may use requestAnimationFrame, but capture must call seek(t) for each requested frame. Use fixed initial state and closed-form or explicitly bounded easing. Keep the icon centered with enough margin for small viewports; keep stroke widths, corner radii, and text sizes consistent. Do not use pointer/cursor/caret overlays, click demonstrations, generic UI chrome gradients, unrelated particles, glow halos, mismatched icon strokes, or a template-like layout.

For a transparent asset, render against a known, uniform matte color and retain that color in the evidence. Use a verified unpremultiply/matting path before claiming true alpha. Do not switch to green or magenta chroma key, and do not claim that an H.264 MP4 contains transparency. If the alpha path is unavailable, deliver the opaque MP4 with its background status stated.

Mandatory Chromium-to-FFmpeg pipeline

Run these stages in order. Keep the source HTML, frame directory, and logs until verification is complete.

Check the actual runtime. Confirm a usable headless Chromium/Playwright, ffmpeg, and ffprobe. Start the page through a local HTTP server when file:// would change loading behavior. If a dependency is missing, report it; do not invent a binary path or silently use a different recorder.

Run browser QA. Load the real page in headless Chromium, wait for fonts and supplied assets, and fail on page errors. Exercise seek(0), one middle beat, seek(duration), reset, and the smallest requested viewport. Capture one still per confirmed beat before the full render and inspect icon readability/crowding.

Record frame by frame. For i = 0..FRAME_COUNT-1, evaluate window.seek(i / FPS) in Chromium, wait for the page to settle without using wall-clock animation, and screenshot the exact viewport to frames/%05d.png. The frame count is finite and known before recording.

Encode with FFmpeg. A spec-mode visual encode has the following bounded shape; substitute the confirmed dimensions and output path:

If audio is requested, it is optional and independent of the visual grid. Use only a contiguous, direct trim; do not audition, parse, fingerprint, infer BPM, build a waveform, beat-match, peak-align, remix, or time-stretch it:

Keep source/license/access evidence for an audio file. If BPM is not declared by the source, record unknown; never derive it from the file.

Enforce a watchdog. The host process must time out below the five-minute gateway limit (use about 240s), send SIGTERM, allow a short grace period, then send SIGKILL. Delete incomplete output and mark the render failed after timeout. A still-running shell or child process is not success.

Verification and delivery

Run the checks that match the requested output and report each tier separately:

Source/static: HTML/JS syntax, asset loading, and any available focused checks. Verify that DURATION, FPS, and frame count are explicit.
Browser: no console/page errors; initial, middle, final, reset, narrow viewport, and reduced-motion behavior where applicable; beat stills reviewed.
Media decode: decode the MP4 with FFmpeg and inspect it with ffprobe. Confirm duration is <= 5.000s, frame count is exactly the planned finite count, FPS and dimensions match, audio is bounded when present, and there are no black or missing frames. A successful FFmpeg exit alone is insufficient.
Loop: compare the rendered seek(0) and seek(DURATION) states. Confirm the encoded final frame is the last planned frame and that no frame 301 exists.
Canvas export: only when the user explicitly requests it, use the current TapNow CLI help/schema to upload the verified MP4 and reread the created Canvas node for source, duration, dimensions, and playable state. Do not upload HTML, a browser Blob, a render plan, or an unverified recording.

Label each delivered artifact as one of source code, beat grid,, render plan, opaque MP4, transparent asset, or verified MP4. State which checks passed, which were blocked, and what remains unverified. If a hard limit, dependency, source/rights gate, decode check, frame count, or loop check fails, stop and report that state instead of calling the result complete.

Reference boundary

This workflow adapts the public 3dicon pattern of one approved still, a single physical motion proposal, first/last state closure, and known-background edge handling to TapNow's deterministic HTML capture path. It deliberately keeps the TapNow runtime boundary explicit: the reference's model/provider and Python CLI are not assumed to exist here. Use only tools and models exposed by the current TapNow Agent runtime.

Use the six-section full-reference structure for the default multi-reference route: subject_definitions, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape, and non_diegetic_music.
Cite each reference as {{node/<id>}}. A citation keeps one meaning throughout.
On the full-reference route, state whether each visible reference is identity, 仅供参考, transferred, or weakly referenced — and for 仅供参考, what it may lend and must not; state whether audio is copied or referenced.
Preserve user dialogue, lyrics, and visible text exactly. Keep speaker IDs stable and place exact spoken content inside <d>[Language] ...</d>.
Describe camera motion as type plus meaningful speed and amplitude, inside the relevant shot rather than as a decorative keyword list.
Separate diegetic ambience and physical sounds from audience-only music.
Use the first/last-frame alignment instruction on the first/last route; those stills are the endpoints, not 仅供参考.
Never add unsupported model parameters to the prompt.
Output Contract

For prompt or storyboard work, return:

Creative intent — one sentence and the primary acceptance criterion.
Confirmed setup — target duration, aspect/destination when known, mode, and immutable locks.
Reference Role Map — every asset in confirmed order and its authority.
Timeline — complete contiguous ranges.
Final H3 prompt — exact model-ready prompt with no competing alternative.
Review checklist — three to six observable checks.
Controlled retry — one variable to change if the first pass fails.

For direct generation, pass the final prompt unchanged to the runtime workflow and answer in product terms. For diagnosis, identify the visible failure, likely causal instruction, smallest rewrite, preserve list, and one retry variable.

Quality Bar
Prefer causal, chronological direction over adjective density.
Give each reference one explicit job and each timeline range one dominant event.
Make motion readable through anticipation, contact, response, and recovery.
Keep one coherent camera intent per range.
End on a concrete composition, object state, expression, UI state, or audio resolution.
Protect exact identity, product truth, geometry, copy, dialogue, and rights.
Separate concept footage from engine-ready game assets, verified UI, factual evidence, or real captured gameplay.
Do not turn provider claims, community examples, or popularity into TapNow runtime guarantees.

name: html-beat-morph-video
text:
返回
html-beat-morph-video

html-beat-morph-video

TapNow

Use when creating a deterministic HTML/CSS/JavaScript motion video in which one visual subject morphs across beat-synced states for UI, product or commercial promotion, technology launches, brand/data explainers, or similar short-form visual communication, and must render as a bounded seamless loop of no more than 5.000 seconds.

HTML Beat Morph Video
Overview

Turn one visual subject or connected composition into a sequence of morphing states and render it as a beat-driven, pure-HTML video loop. UI remains a supported recipe, but the same motion grammar also covers product/commercial promos, technology launch films, brand openers, data or concept explainers, and short social title pieces. Preserve the original single-subject, state-order, pure-seek(t), and rendering framework; the default is 120 BPM, 10 beats, and 5.000 seconds. Keep this entrypoint short and load detailed capability from references/ only when needed.

Interaction gate
Use the user's language for questions, state grids, visible copy, and delivery notes: English input gets English by default; Chinese input gets Chinese by default unless the user explicitly requests another copy language.
Take the shortest path to collect three inputs: 8–12 desired visual states or beats, pure black and white or one accent color, and a royalty-free, commercial-use song. The 120 BPM value belongs to the visual grid; never verify it from the audio file. States may be UI components, product surfaces or features, device or packaging silhouettes, technical diagrams, data motifs, brand/title moments, or other supplied visual subjects. Prefer one targeted Mixkit search; do not add unrelated explanation or play the song.
Duration is not a normal input: default 5.000s, hard maximum 5.000s. Canvas dimensions may follow the user's request; use square 1440×1440 when unspecified. Never ask for or propose more than 5 seconds.
Show the complete state list and time grid before writing code and wait for explicit confirmation. If the user asks for the fastest path, use canonical states and one Mixkit candidate as provisional defaults and ask one compact confirmation; never skip the confirmation gate.
The 10-beat slots, one event per beat, single-subject morphing, and return to the first frame are fixed framework rules. Map the user's 8–12 state candidates into the fixed slots; do not move beat points or add an eleventh beat.
Duration and runtime boundary
The default/spec mode is 5.000s, 10 beats, 500ms/beat, 60fps, and 300 frames.
A shorter duration or different dimensions is allowed, but preserve state order, beat-driven changes, pure time evaluation, and loop identity; every mode must be ≤ 5.000s. Only spec mode simultaneously uses 120 BPM / 500ms beat / 10 beats; a shorter mode must explicitly reduce slots or recompute beat interval/BPM in the confirmation grid and must not claim to remain 10×500ms.
The 5-second cap is also a system-performance guard: longer videos are more likely to fail in browser rendering, encoding, or gateway streaming. Do not extend duration to solve crowding; compress a state or adjust the configurable dimensions.
Immutable output rules
One visual subject morphs continuously; do not cut between scenes. seek(end) and seek(0) must have identical subject geometry, label or title, radius or silhouette, color, and settled spring values.
Output obeys the requested duration with 0 < duration ≤ 5.000s; spec mode remains 5.000s / 300 frames. Any export, tail frame, audio, or loop beyond the cap fails.
Do not use a pointer, cursor, caret, click, drag hand, fade-out tail, particle burst, glow, UI-chrome gradient, bouncy easing, mismatched icon strokes, dead time, or template-like treatment.
Every FFmpeg synthesis command must be bounded: final output uses -t <video_duration> (optionally with -shortest), apad may only be bounded as apad=pad_dur=...; never use infinite apad, infinite tail audio, or a Gateway 5-minute stream timeout as the stopping mechanism. Give the FFmpeg process a watchdog/abort below 5 minutes, clean up timed-out processes, and remove incomplete output.
Read as needed
Input questions, language, confirmation gate, and configurable parameters: references/input-gate.md [blocked]
One-subagent Mixkit search, license evidence, and source logging: references/mixkit-fast-path.md [blocked]
120 BPM and the complete 10-beat timing table: references/beat-grid.md [blocked]
Single-subject visual direction, camera, font, and bans: references/visual-motion-rules.md [blocked]
Single HTML, configurable dimensions, pure seek(t), closed-form springs, and morph implementation: references/seek-spring-implementation.md [blocked]
Direct audio trim, no audio analysis, no playback, Playwright, bounded FFmpeg/watchdog, and frame output: references/audio-render-pipeline.md [blocked]
Text timing, will-change, loop identity, timeout, and final checks: references/qa-gotchas.md [blocked]
Delivery order

Confirm the grid first. Then use one Mixkit subagent to find and log a candidate, implement the single HTML and audio, directly trim the selected track to the confirmed window, render one still per confirmed beat slot, fix timing/crowding/readability, and run the bounded full render under a watchdog. Do not parse, analyze, audition, beat-match, or peak-align the music; the visual grid is independent of the audio. When requested, deliver the HTML, video, and audio source/license record. Acceptance covers state order, timing, direct audio window, frame count, FFmpeg boundedness, and loop identity.

name: digital-human-video
text:
返回
digital-human-video

digital-human-video

TapNow

Use when creating a presenter-led digital-human video for a product, property, lesson, knowledge explainer, social message, course, market bulletin, or news bulletin, especially when it needs a consistent presenter, visual B-roll, HTML screen recordings, or Canvas export.

Digital Human Video

Use one shared presenter workflow and route-specific video methods. This package contains all routing, identity, and execution instructions; do not invoke another Skill, open Casting Room, or create an MCP App to complete a route.

Route the user's query

Infer the desired result from the current query, supplied material, and prior approved work. Choose by the viewer's job, not by a matching platform or topic word. Read only the selected route reference, plus shared references when needed.

Route	User's intended result	Example query	Read
asset	Create/save a reusable presenter or fill an existing Element's Look/voice gaps	"Create a digital human first, add an office look, and do not make a video"	Asset method [blocked]
social	A short direct-to-camera message, announcement, or general social explanation	"Have the digital human deliver this script as a Reels talking-head video"	Social method [blocked]
property	Help viewers evaluate or visit a specific real property, venue, or facility with guide-to-space cutaways	"Make a TikTok video introducing this hotel"	Property method [blocked]
product	Demonstrate/promote a product's value, feature, or use with presenter-to-product cutaways and product evidence	"Have a digital human demo this app's new feature and end with a trial call to action"	Product method [blocked]
course	Teach a skill or process with an observable learning outcome, alternating on-camera presenter delivery and teaching visuals	"Teach new users how to export a report in this app"	Course method [blocked]
market	Explain dated developments, trends, or changes using sources and data	"Report this week's property-market changes"	Market method [blocked]
news	Report current events or a news story from network-searched sources with source-labelled visual evidence	"Report today's AI industry news"	News method [blocked]

Apply these precedence rules:

A local revision stays with its existing route. "Only change the CTA" or "Replace the second shot" reuses the existing brief, presenter, and accepted assets. Ask for the target artifact only if it cannot be identified; do not restart onboarding.

Explicit outcomes outrank channel and subject. A TikTok hotel tour is property; a property-market update is market; a current-event bulletin is news; a software lesson is course; a persuasive software launch demo is product. General short speech is social when a more specific outcome does not apply.

Missing identity is a prerequisite, not a route change. "There is no person yet; make a product demo" remains product with the shared production sequence below. Create or reuse its character subject without adding an unrequested actor package, multiple Looks, or voice library.

Combine only requested deliverables. If the user requests a tour and a market update, plan two deliverables under property and market, reuse the adopted presenter, and keep each script, evidence ledger, and output state separate. If they request a reusable presenter plus a video, use the shared sequence once; saving the subject also fulfills the asset deliverable.

Ask one outcome question only when needed. For an ambiguous "product walkthrough", use the CTA, audience, and supplied script to distinguish promotion from instruction. If still unresolved, ask whether viewers should choose the product or learn to complete a task. Do not make users select internal route names or six modules.

Object and space outcomes require cutaways. A product or property brief that contains a physical product, software interface, room, venue, building, or amenity must include a shot plan with presenter A-roll and subject cutaways. Do not deliver an all-presenter talking head when the viewer needs to inspect the thing being introduced. social and market stay presenter-led unless their brief explicitly requests supporting inserts.

Course outcomes require teaching visuals. A course brief must map each learning beat to on-camera presenter A-roll, GPT-generated explanatory B-roll, deterministic HTML/CSS/JS recording, supplied capture, or uploaded B-roll. When a visual carries the concept, alternate A-roll and B-roll in the shot plan and read Course method [blocked]; do not deliver an all-presenter lesson or an unordered asset list.

News outcomes require network research and recorded evidence. A news brief must search the network before scripting, preserve a source ledger and cut-off time, and render source-labelled HTML evidence as B-roll. Every HTML-to-video path must use the installed ffmpeg and headless Chromium chain; read News method [blocked] and do not present search snippets, stale pages, or an all-presenter bulletin as the finished news deliverable.

The route is internal planning state. Explain the intended deliverable in the user's language. If the request falls outside these outcomes, explain the scope instead of forcing it into a digital-human workflow.

Shared presenter gate

Inspect explicit attachments and selected Canvas/Element references. Reuse an authorized single-person identity that the user has chosen; never select the latest node, a filename, or a person from a group photo by inference. The identity gate is the visual anchor only; it does not approve the keyframe previs, voice, character subject, or video.

For a local revision, reuse the identity recorded in the existing project. A text or overlay-only edit that creates no new presenter media does not reopen this gate.

If no person is supplied, read Presenter identity [blocked]: one ordinary show_form, exact account-available Midjourney v8.2, a 2:3 headshot on #808080, a short English prompt ending in --style raw, exact-result inspection, then explicit user adoption. Do not require a provider output count or reject a supported Midjourney result because of its returned shape. Use the route's live structured parameters for ratio, resolution, and quality. Do not use a beauty fallback or nearby-version fallback.

Keep the selected business route while waiting. Before identity adoption, do not generate presenter media. Already supplied facts and copy remain inputs; never discard or recollect them. Once adopted, the same exact face reference serves every route.

Required production sequence

For a new presenter-led video, keep this order. Skip a stage only when its approved artifact already exists and is still valid for the requested change.

Lock the brief and aspect. Collect audience, objective, script or topic, duration, and orientation. Use landscape 16:9 or portrait 9:16 according to the brief; if it is genuinely ambiguous, ask before generating. Resolve the live model contract for the exact ratio instead of guessing a provider parameter.

Create the visual identity. Reuse an explicitly approved person or follow Presenter identity [blocked] to use Midjourney v8.2 for the raw headshot. The prompt must describe one person and one casting headshot; do not turn it into multiple casting options or enumerate candidate identities. Inspect the result(s) returned by the live route and wait for explicit adoption of one face anchor; keep that anchor fixed afterward.

Select and fix the voice. Reuse an approved voice. For a user-designated upload, inspect its exact audio reference and bind it as voice_ref; an explicit request to use that voice counts as selection. Do not generate alternative voices for it. Otherwise resolve the newest available Seed Audio model, generate a small voice candidate set (default two) using the same short audition line, let the user listen and choose, and bind that result as voice_ref. Use fast, clear speech and lively intonation. Read the live model contract before generating; do not hard-code an assumed latest version. Keep this voice identity for every subsequent audio job.

Build and confirm the keyframe scene. After the face and voice are approved, use the live GPT 2.5 model contract to make the minimum keyframe previs for the requested scene(s), with the selected person, scene, action, framing, and locked 16:9 or 9:16 ratio. Pass the adopted face as the identity reference; describe a real human in a live-action scene. For product and property, include the subject in the keyframe plan: presenter framing, presenter_with_object or presenter_in_space when the relation matters, product/space hero, close-up or detail, and the return to the presenter. Generate one keyframe per distinct composition. For course, cover the presenter, concept_visual, worked_example, and any screen_demo or html_recording frame required by the learning beat. For news, cover the news_anchor, headline/source card, timeline, chart/map/quote frame, and return to the anchor needed by the source claims. A continuous shot can reuse its approved keyframe across several audio segments. Use a few concise sentences for person, action, framing, setting, object/space detail, and light. Put aspect, count, and quality in supported structured parameters. Inspect the exact person-in-scene and subject keyframes and get explicit approval.

Create the character subject. Only after the keyframe scene is approved, create or update the character subject/Element through the current persistence contract. Bind the adopted face, selected voice_ref, approved scene/keyframe references, and only the requested Look assets. Preserve unrelated members.

Generate the first talking scene. Prepare the first scene's spoken audio with the selected Seed Audio voice anchor with fast delivery and lively, varied intonation, then use Seedance 2.5 for the first talking-video segment and the continuation workflow. Seedance 2.0 or MiniMax H3 remain alternatives for separate video requests when selected by the user; never silently switch an explicitly chosen model. The video prompt must require a real human presenter, fast but clear speech, varied expressions that follow the meaning, natural eye contact, head movements, and gestures. Bind the character subject, approved keyframe, scene-one audio, exact spoken copy, locked aspect, and timing. For product and property, generate presenter and cutaway source clips as separate shot units, then assemble their approved order on the timeline. For course, generate presenter A-roll and each teaching B-roll unit separately; record approved HTML/CSS/JS visuals before assembly and export the assembled lesson timeline to Canvas through the supported path. Inspect the exact completed first scene and its first teaching or subject cutaway before continuing. For news, search and verify the source ledger before writing the final lines, then generate the presenter A-roll and source-labelled HTML B-roll separately. Any HTML-to-video recording must use the installed ffmpeg and headless Chromium chain before the assembled bulletin is exported to Canvas.

 

Reuse this compact performance clause in each video prompt, then add only the scene-specific action and continuity details:

Make the next scene audio and extend. After the first scene is accepted, generate the next scene's audio with the same voice_ref and the current Seed Audio contract. Extend the continuous presenter A-roll in Seedance 2.5 using the immediately preceding accepted presenter video, the new scene audio, the same subject, and supported scene/keyframe context. For product and property, put approved B-roll over the A-roll in the final timeline. For course, place each approved teaching visual under the matching voice_span; HTML recordings and source captures remain independent B-roll unless the live contract explicitly supports their continuation. Only use a direct A→B or B→A video continuation when the live contract explicitly supports that shot-type change; otherwise generate the B-roll independently and keep its voiceover span in the renderer manifest. Scene 2 uses scene 1's accepted predecessor, scene 3 uses scene 2's accepted predecessor, and so on. Keep voice, aspect, and performance consistent. Follow the runtime contract for continuity, output overlap, and audio timing; stop when the complete approved script has been spoken and the requested deliverable is covered. For news, keep the source-labelled HTML B-roll independent unless the live contract explicitly supports a shot-type change, and assemble it under the matching verified news voice_span.

Product and property cutaway layer

Read the selected Product method [blocked] or Property method [blocked] for the route-specific shot grammar. The shared rule is:

Keep presenter speech, product/space visuals, and sourced proof as separate shot units. A cutaway may carry the continuing approved voiceover, but it must not be hidden inside a talking-head generation prompt.
Give every shot a shot_type, source_ref, script_span, voice_span, duration, transition point, and acceptance state. Use presenter for A-roll, presenter_with_object or presenter_in_space for a person-subject relationship, object_hero or object_detail for product views, demo_action for use, and space_wide, space_detail, or amenity for property views.
Alternate on purpose: presenter establishes the claim, the product or space proves it visually, and the presenter returns for interpretation or CTA. Do not cut on every sentence or use an insert that has no spoken or evidentiary role.
Generate object/space clips separately from presenter clips. For a real product, UI, address, room, amenity, measurement, label, or price, use supplied or captured source media whenever exact appearance matters. Generated subject footage is illustrative until matched to an approved source. Keep pure B-roll prompts short: object/space, shot size, action, light, and continuity detail. Use the real-human, fast, expressive performance clause only for presenter or presenter_with_object shots, never for a product/space-only closeup.
Assemble only after the individual clips and their audio spans are approved. Check that cuts preserve the fixed person, product identity, spatial orientation, speech continuity, safe areas, and readable labels. An ordered clip list is partial when a rendered master was requested.
Course teaching B-roll layer

Read the selected Course method [blocked] for the full teaching contract. The shared rule is:

Keep on-camera presenter A-roll and teaching B-roll as separate shot units. Use presenter for goals, explanations, judgment, correction, recap, and practice; use presenter_with_visual when the relationship between the person and visual is itself instructional.
Use concept_visual for an illustrative GPT visual, html_recording for exact UI/code/formula/chart/table/timeline states, screen_demo for supplied or captured procedures, worked_example for sourced calculations, and caption_card for exact definitions or warnings. Do not use generated imagery as an exact UI, live-data, official-chart, or completed-experiment substitute.
Give every teaching unit a learning_step or claim_id, visual_mode, source_ref or html_artifact_ref, script_span, voice_span, duration, cut-in/cut-out, evidence_role, and review_state. For HTML, also record the artifact version, viewport, frame rate, duration, start/end state, and recording reference before export.
Keep approved voiceover under silent B-roll only within its matching voice_span; return to on-camera presenter delivery for interpretation, correction, emphasis, recap, or the next action. Cut on a teaching event such as a visual reveal, code action, formula change, or worked result instead of cutting only for variety.
Export the assembled course timeline to Canvas through the supported renderer or write-back path and read back the returned Canvas reference. An HTML preview, local recording, A-roll clip set, or unordered B-roll list is partial when a lesson video was requested.
News bulletin layer

Read the selected News method [blocked] before planning a news video. News is a source-verification and visual-evidence route, not a generic market or talking-head route:

Search the network before writing the final script or generating news visuals. Fix the source cutoff time, timezone, geography, language, audience, and freshness window. Prefer primary sources, then independently corroborate material claims. Keep facts, source claims, interpretation, and unresolved items separate.
Give every claim a source URL/document, title, publication or update time, search and access time, source type, status, exact source span, and claim_id. A 403, login wall, missing date, or stale page is an access/freshness gap, not proof that no update exists.
Use a deliberate A/B sequence: news_anchor says what happened, source-labelled HTML B-roll shows the headline, timeline, chart, map, quote, or source strip, and the anchor returns to explain impact, uncertainty, or the next item. Keep each B-roll unit tied to one verified claim_id and voice_span.
Any HTML-to-video or page-recording path is fixed to the installed stack: ffmpeg and headless Chromium are installed. Headless Chromium renders the deterministic page at the locked viewport; ffmpeg encodes or packages the captured frames and audio into video. A browser preview, HTML file, or search-result screenshot is not a finished video. Record browser/ffmpeg versions, viewport, fps, duration, start/end state, output reference, source cutoff, and Canvas reference.
Export the assembled bulletin to Canvas and read back the returned reference. If network search, source ledger, fixed-stack recording, or Canvas write-back is unavailable, report the news result as partial and preserve the exact gap.

Do not add a separate image or exploratory keyframe generation stage solely to create selection candidates, and do not force a provider-specific image count. Keep the Midjourney prompt focused on one person; use the result shape returned by the live route and bind only the image the user explicitly adopts as the face anchor. Voice candidates remain the intentional selection set. If a visual, voice, or video result is rejected, regenerate only that stage after the user supplies a changed direction; keep approved stages and references unchanged.

Use "real human" and positive performance direction in generation prompts. Do not label the subject “digital human”, “AI avatar”, or “virtual presenter”, even in a stock negative clause. Avoid stiff posture, frozen expressions, mechanical nodding, or looping gestures in the result. This describes the desired visual performance; retain truthful synthetic-media context in delivery.

Shared execution
Establish the brief. Read the selected route's method, reuse known inputs, and collect only blocking gaps: audience, objective, exact facts/source media, script or prompt, orientation, duration, voice, and final deliverables.
Plan the staged artifacts. Preserve supplied exact copy. For a topic prompt, produce the full spoken script, compact GPT 2.5 presenter/subject keyframe prompts, shot plan, cutaway and teaching-visual source list, per-claim source ledger, and per-scene audio lines before generation. For course, choose a visual mode for every beat (gpt_visual, html_recording, source_capture, or uploaded_broll) before generation. For news, complete network search and the source ledger before final script, HTML, or A-roll generation. Reuse existing approval for unchanged work. Asset-only requests follow asset.md and do not enter video production.
Record dependencies. Track route, aspect, identity reference/state, keyframe references, approved script, voice candidates and selected voice_ref, character subject, facts/sources, scene ids, shot types, cutaway source refs, spoken lines/audio results, media/reference roles, overlay/caption text, teaching learning_step/claim_id, visual mode, HTML artifact and recording references, news source URL/title/published-at/accessed-at/status/cutoff fields, browser and ffmpeg versions, viewport, fps, timing, cut order, segment chain, exact job/result references, Canvas export and read-back references, review state, and export state. This is a project manifest, not a new Element schema or backend API.
Execute the current contract. Read Runtime contract [blocked] before generation, media inspection, persistence, or rendering. Use standard TapNow CLI and existing forms. For every HTML-to-video/page-recording task, verify the installed stack exactly as ffmpeg and headless Chromium are installed before capture; do not substitute a browser preview or an untracked recorder. A source reference, submitted job, completed media result, inspected result, and final export are distinct states.
Review the smallest changed unit. Keep the face anchor, keyframes, voice, and accepted assets fixed. Re-render changed information cards without regenerating the presenter; regenerate a spoken line only when speech changed. Changing a scene's audio regenerates that scene's video. A changed video invalidates downstream continuations that used it as their source; preserve earlier scenes and recheck or regenerate affected continuations. A new identity invalidates dependent presenter visuals; a new voice invalidates dependent speech and talking video. For product or property work, a changed object/space source invalidates only the affected cutaway and any downstream assembly that depends on its timing. For course, a changed claim, formula, code result, HTML artifact, source capture, or learning step invalidates its teaching shot, narration/caption timing, and dependent assembly, while preserving unrelated chapters. For news, a changed source, cutoff, claim, date, number, quote, or HTML evidence card invalidates that claim's source ledger row, A-roll line, B-roll recording, captions, and dependent assembly.
Deliver the real result. Match the requested asset or video scope. A full business video requires an actual assembled export; an A-roll clip or ordered segment set is partial when assembly was requested. Report missing runtime capabilities and remaining work precisely. Do not publish externally.
Interaction and acceptance
Keep form submission, identity adoption, voice confirmation, keyframe-previs approval, subject creation, platform cost confirmation, and final review separate. Honor authorization already given for the same scope; do not stack duplicate forms or add confirmation at every scene.
Preserve the presenter's truthful role. Generated presenters do not create evidence of customer experience, credentials, real locations, product performance, or financial outcomes. Apply the selected route's specific evidence rules.
Inspect exact completed media for identity continuity, fixed voice, complete speech, lip sync, fast clear delivery, expressive natural movement, facts, caption/chart legibility, teaching order, HTML/screen readability, timing, cut order, cutaway continuity, product/space identity, news source ledger and cutoff, publication/ access times, fixed ffmpeg + headless Chromium recording state, Canvas export state, safe areas, and the CTA or next learning action. Frozen faces, stiff movement, repeated gestures, voice drift, unexplained cuts, or skipped/repeated lines fail review. State which checks could not run; structural validation alone is not visual acceptance.
Deliver exact asset/media references, the script or captions when relevant, sources/rights and synthetic-presenter context, unresolved items, and the actual export status. Do not promise virality, sales, or guaranteed outcomes.

name: depth-video-studio
text:
返回
depth-video-studio

depth-video-studio

TapNow

The depth-video workflow skill. Reuse an existing clip's motion, staging and camera while replacing who is in it and where it happens. Convert the source clip into a depth-map video, confirm the new character and the new setting with the user, then generate a fresh video that follows the depth pass for movement and the new references for appearance. Use whenever the user asks for a depth video, a depth map or depth pass of a clip, for the same camera move or the same action performed by a different character, for swapping the person or the background of a video they already have, or for recasting or relocating an existing shot.

Depth Video Studio

Take a clip the user already has, keep what is expensive to re-author — the movement, the timing, the spatial depth and the camera path — and replace what they actually want changed: the character and the setting. The mechanism is a two-stage chain. A depth-map pass turns the source clip into a per-frame grayscale depth video that carries motion and space but no identity; a second generation then treats that depth video as the motion authority and the new images as the appearance authority.

The deliverables are the depth video node, the recast video node, and the reference role map and prompt that produced them. All three stay on the canvas, so later variants reuse the same depth pass instead of paying for it again.

When This Is The Right Shape
The user points at a clip and wants the same action, blocking or camera move performed by someone else, somewhere else.
The user asks directly for a depth map, depth pass or depth video, whether or not a recast follows.
The motion already exists and is worth preserving. When the user is inventing motion from scratch, build a whitebox instead and use whitebox-to-film; when they want the source clip itself edited in place rather than re-performed, use the host's video edit route instead of a depth chain.

One depth pass serves many recasts. When the user asks for another character or another setting on a clip already converted in this conversation, reuse the existing depth node and go straight to the second generation.

Stage 1 — The Depth Pass

Read the source clip before converting it. Look at the actual media, not just the node title: what the subject does, how the camera moves, how long the clip runs and what its frame is. That observation is what lets you write an honest role map later, and it is what tells you whether the motion is worth preserving at all.

Then read the depth model's live contract before submitting — accepted method, reference count and resolution options belong to the model, not to this skill. Depth conversion is a pure transform: it takes exactly one video, keeps the source length, and does not read the prompt, so the prompt is a short note and nothing about the desired final look belongs in it. Keep the source resolution unless the user asked otherwise.

Submitting opens a confirmation card and suspends the run. Wait for the real decision. See Generating and Chaining [blocked] for what to do while waiting, how to tell when the depth video is actually ready, and how to handle a rejection.

Stage 2 — Ask What Changes

The depth pass fixes movement and space. Everything the user cares about — who and where — is still open, and guessing it wastes a generation. Ask, but ask only for what the canvas and the conversation cannot already answer.

The answer must be expressible both as a picked canvas asset and as a description in words. A user who already has the character on the canvas should point at it; a user who only has an idea should type it. A choice card built from fixed text options supports neither well, and is the wrong tool here.

Read Asking What To Change [blocked] before choosing an elicitation surface. It covers which surface carries canvas references, how to build image options from canvas nodes, what to infer instead of ask, and how to accept an answer that arrives as a node reference in ordinary conversation.

Stage 3 — The Recast Generation

Look at every reference before writing the prompt, including the depth video you just produced. A depth pass that came back mostly flat, or that lost the subject, is a stage 1 problem and re-prompting stage 2 will not fix it.

Choose a model whose live contract offers a multi-reference video mode, and read that contract for the reference budget per media kind and for the duration, frame and resolution options. Two things routinely surprise users:

The recast is not length-locked to the depth video. The depth pass keeps the source length, but the new generation's duration is an independent parameter with its own default and its own ceiling. When the user wants the whole clip recast, set the duration to the source length and say so if the model cannot reach it.
Defaults are not the user's request. Resolution, aspect ratio and audio all have model defaults that quietly differ from what the user asked for. Set explicitly what the user stated; leave the rest at the model default rather than inventing values.

When the chosen model has its own prompt copilot skill, let it own the prompt's wording and craft; this skill owns the chain, the role map and the reference order, and those constraints survive into whatever prompt that copilot writes.

The prompt's whole job is to assign authority. Each reference gets one thing it controls and an explicit statement of what it must not contribute — above all that the depth video supplies motion, staging and spatial depth and must not contribute its grayscale rendering. Reference order matters: the submitted request rewrites node placeholders into ordinal labels per media kind, so the order references are passed is the order the prompt's roles must follow. See Reference Roles and Prompting [blocked].

Delivery
Say which clip supplied the motion, which references supplied identity and setting, and what was generated at what duration and resolution. The user should be able to tell from the reply alone why the new video moves the way it does.
Name the real differences from the source: a recast follows the depth pass, it does not reproduce the original frame for frame, and duration or frame may have changed.
When the result inherits the grayscale, loses the character's identity or keeps the old background, fix it at the layer that caused it — see the failure table in Reference Roles and Prompting [blocked]. Do not resubmit an unchanged request hoping for a different sample.
Do not claim a node was created, bound or completed without the submission result that proves it, and do not describe the depth video as the deliverable when the user asked for the recast.
在对话中使用
description: The depth-video workflow skill. Reuse an existing clip's motion, staging and camera while replacing who is in it and where it happens. Convert the source clip into a depth-map video, confirm the new character and the new setting with the user, then generate a fresh video that follows the depth pass for movement and the new references for appearance. Use whenever the user asks for a depth video, a depth map or depth pass of a clip, for the same camera move or the same action performed by a different character, for swapping the person or the background of a video they already have, or for recasting or relocating an existing shot.

name: commerce-ad-studio
text:
返回
commerce-ad-studio

commerce-ad-studio

TapNow

The e-commerce ad creative workflow skill. Starting from what the user already has — product photos, an approved ad, a reference video, customer reviews or campaign results — make or adapt ad creative for that product. Covers localizing a static ad for other countries with translated copy and local typography, resizing it for other placements, multiplying headline variants of one image or hook variants of one video for A/B tests, recreating a reference ad's structure and pacing as an original ad for the user's product, turning real customer feedback into a faceless voiced ad video, planning ad angles from product and competitor research, reading campaign results into scale, pause and test decisions, and animating product or brand material as illustration, paper collage, whiteboard, deck or app-screen motion. Use whenever the user wants ads or marketing creative made, adapted, varied, localized or planned for a product, even when they name only one of these jobs.

Commerce Ad Studio

Every job here has the same shape. The user brings a source — product photos, an ad they already run, a reference video, reviews, a results table. Some things about it are fixed: the product's look, the brand, the offer, what may be claimed. One thing changes: the language, the size, the headline, the opening seconds, the product inside a borrowed structure. Write both lists down before anything is generated. Almost every bad result in ad work is a fixed thing that quietly changed, or two things that changed when the user asked for one.

Pick the job
The user wants	Job	Stays fixed	Changes	Read
The ad for other countries or languages	Localize	product, brand, offer terms, layout family	copy, typography, number and currency formats	static ads [blocked]
The ad in other sizes or placements	Resize	message, copy, product	aspect and layout	static ads [blocked]
Several headlines on one ad, to test	Headline variants	everything outside the headline	the headline	static ads [blocked]
Several openings on one video, to test	Hook variants	body, ending, offer	the first seconds	video ads [blocked]
"One like this video" for their product	Recreate	the reference's selling structure and pacing — nothing else	footage, words, product: all new	video ads [blocked]
An ad from real reviews, nobody on screen, with a voice	Customer voice	the customers' real words, the product facts	—	video ads [blocked]
A video ad in other languages	Localize video	picture and key timing	voice, captions, on-screen copy	video ads [blocked]
What to say, which angles, what competitors do	Strategy	verified facts	—	strategy and analysis [blocked]
What the campaign numbers mean and what to do next	Analysis	read-only	—	strategy and analysis [blocked]
Illustration, collage, whiteboard, a deck, app screens or brand assets set in motion	Motion	the source art, exact copy, facts	movement	motion formats [blocked]

Read the reference for the job before planning it, and only that one. A request that fits no row still takes the same shape: name the source, the fixed list and the one change. A coherent listing photo set — white-background main image, feature, detail and lifestyle shots — is a product-image-set job, not an ad job; this skill takes an image from such a set as its source.

Jobs chain. Strategy yields concepts; a chosen concept becomes the control for headline variants; the winner gets resized, then localized. Run one job at a time and let it land before the next starts: the output of one is the source of the next, and a change upstream sends everything downstream back to draft.

Product truth before copy

Every visible word in an ad is a claim the user's business answers for. Read Product Truth [blocked] before writing any copy. Price, discount, shipping promise, certification, rating, result and customer quote come from the user or from a source you can name — never from what would sound persuasive.

Ask once, for what blocks

Look first: the conversation, the Canvas, attachments, the Library — the user may already keep a product dossier or earlier ads there. Then ask only for what this job cannot proceed without, in one surface:

show_form for several facts at once — target markets, placements, number of variants, the offer per market. Use image_select to pick which ad or product photo is the source; it takes images only, so a video source is picked by title in a select field. Put the default you would assume on every field and a companion text field wherever your options might miss. After showing a form, end the turn and wait for the submission.
A choice between creative alternatives whose text is heavy — two recreated scripts, five angles — is a show_widget decision panel with one button per alternative.
AskUserQuestion only for a blocking choice whose options are exhaustive: translate or transcreate, dub or subtitle.

Facts, the choice of a concept, and the go-ahead to generate are separate decisions; never fold them into one yes. Copy is the user's words — offer versions, let them pick and edit, and generate only approved copy.

Making

Generation follows the Making contract in your instructions unchanged: available models, the model's described contract, two-pass confirmation, recovery after a failure. This skill adds:

The source is a reference with a job. The prompt says what it controls and what it must not contribute — "keep everything in the referenced ad: product, layout, colors, background, every other line of text; replace only the headline with …". The one exception is a Recreate reference video, which is analysed and never passed.
Exact text is quoted exactly. Approved copy goes into the prompt one string per text zone. After generation, read every visible character back from the image against the approved copy — a wrong accent, a dropped character, an extra word — and treat any mismatch as a failed take, never a deliverable.
Variants of one job are one batch: same model, same parameters, only the prompt and per-item references differ, so the user confirms them on one card. Different aspect ratios are different batches.
A model's prompt copilot skill, when one exists, owns the wording. This skill owns the fixed list, the change and the reference roles; they survive into whatever prompt the copilot writes.
Nothing here joins clips. When a job needs pieces combined — a new hook onto the old body, a voiceover over picture, captions on top — deliver the pieces plus an edit list with exact timecodes, and say the final cut is assembled in their editor. Never call pieces a finished ad.
Judging and delivering

Look at every result before calling it done. Check the fixed list first — product shape, logo, colors, offer, layout, the untouched text — then the one thing meant to change. A variant where two things changed is a failed variant however good it looks; retry it with the drift named in the prompt, never with an unchanged roll.

Deliver in the shape the user will use:

On the Canvas, one group per job, each output titled by what varies: "DE · 4:5", "标题 C · 痛点型", "Hook B · 演示开场".
In the project record's plan, a variant table: variant, the one change, the hypothesis it tests, node, state — and for tests, what to measure.
Anything that exists only as a spec — an edit list, a subtitle script, a copy deck — is labelled as a spec, not as media.

Accepted ads are saved to the project's Library folder, as your instructions describe for accepted work.

3d-scene-director

TapNow

Create and iterate interactive 3D scenes in TapNow from text, images or video, present them through show_widget, and support scene screenshots, recording, file preview and downloads where the environment allows. Also used for explicitly requested 3D scene prompts, shot plans and scene handoff descriptions.
description: Present a 3D scene in the conversation or in an artifact only when the user explicitly asks for that surface. Use show_widget, HTML, or a written prompt or plan. A request to make a 3D scene without that explicit presentation is a 3D Studio node; use `update-3d-studio:update-3d-studio` instead.
